newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL plans to invest HUF 83.8 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: MOL plans to invest HUF 83.8 bln in 1997.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt will invest 83.8 billion forints in 1997, compared with 45.2 billion forints in 1996, company officials said on Friday.
MOL earlier released its 1996 preliminary IAS results showing net income soaring to 22.2 billion forints in 1996 compared with 1.1 billion forints in 1995.
"This was the company's best year ever," MOL's CEO Zoltan Mandoki told a news conference. @
He added that this year MOL will continue its cost-cutting programme, reducing its staff by 1,500 from the 1996 year-end headcount of 14,770.
Hungary's privatisation agency APV said in January it would continue MOL's privatisation in the first half of this year but gave no details.
APV holds a 58 percent stake in MOL, which has issued share capital of 98.4 billion forints and the privatisation law says APV has to retain a 25 percent plus one share stake in the company. @

In answer to a question whether under the new ownership structure he feared that MOL's management would become a buffer between foreign investors' and the state's conflicting interests, he said: "Of course we are afraid, but that's why we are in that position: to handle conflicting interests."
Mandoki denied press reports that MOL has signed a deal with Croatia to buy a minority stake in the Adriatic pipeline saying that some details remain to be clarified.
"Our intentions are serious, but with the main lines of the deal already clear, there are numerous issues that have to be clarified," he said.
Reports out of Zagreb earlier this month said MOL had signed a deal to buy a 12.5 percent stake in the Adriatic pipeline.
"With an investment of this magnitude, one has to be very careful and negotiate the appropriate level of mandates and guarantees," Mandoki said.
He also said that MOL's oil prospecting in Tunisia was successful but could not give any figures.
"Tunisia was a strike and we are assessing the size of it," he said.

MOL's gas business remained loss-making in 1996, as the company bought the gas at world market prices but sold it at state-regulated prices at an average loss of 2.54 forints per cubic metre, Mandoki said.
The January 10 wholesale gas price increase of 16.9 percent was a step in the right direction, but Mandoki said he expected the state to deliver the margins it had promised.
"Gas price regulations are not yet based on market principles," he said. "We hope that regulatory details will ensure...the eight percent return-on-equity stipulated by the law."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, at 1115 GMT, MOL shares stood at 3,185 forints, up 90.
